Subject: Severe p95/p99 spikes on 32k window — urgent

Hi Markus,

We're seeing a major regression in p95/p99 latency from your hosted API starting ~14:30 PDT today. It only shows up for our long-context requests (we run a small batch of 32k-window summarizations overnight) — tail latency is spiking to 10-12s p99 (previously 1.1s). Error rate also increased from 0.2% to 1.5%. This is impacting our nightly reporting jobs and failing SLAs.

Attached is a small sample payload + the request IDs where we saw the worst hits: rreq_33452, rreq_33463, rreq_33479. We're happy to jump on a call — this is high priority for our ops and execs.

Can you confirm receipt and estimated ETA for mitigation?

Thanks,
Tim

Tim — thanks for the rapid flag. I confirm we received your payload and the request ids. Sorry for the disruption. I'm pulling in engineering (Laura + Hannah) and our infra lead (Sergio) to triage immediately.

Immediate short-term options we can take in the next 30–90 minutes while we diagnose:
- Temporarily route Aggie traffic to a dedicated performance pool (isolates workload)
- Enable the fallback model-variant for >16k requests to a quantized, lower-memory variant (fewer KV cache ops)
- Apply a soft throttling policy for concurrent 32k requests to avoid cache blow-up

We should also schedule a 30m war room with your ops and our on-call. Are you available at 16:00 PDT?

I'll follow up with a clear mutual action plan and a short post-mortem.

— Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:35:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Aggie Health — 32k tail latency regression (requests rreq_33452/63/79)

Team — inbound escalation from Aggie (see payload attached). Symptoms:
- p95/p99 increased specifically for 32k-context requests starting ~14:30 PDT
- Error rate uptick correlated with long requests (OOM / timeouts showing in some traces)
- Throughput for that tenant dropped ~40% during the spike window

Initial hypothesis: continuous batching + large KV caches are causing memory pressure on the serving nodes for these long-context sessions; eviction/GC behavior is increasing latency for subsequent requests. There may also be an unexpected kernel/path we hit for >24k token sequences on the currently selected model variant.

Priorities: replication of the issue in staging with the same payloads (Laura), check node-level memory/eviction patterns and RPC queue depths (Sergio), and confirm fallback plan viability (Hannah).

I've attached a perf_trace.json from the customer (they shared sample traces). Please triage and post immediate mitigations within 45m. If we can't stabilize quickly, we'll move to route Aggie to dedicated pool to avoid SLA hits.

— Markus
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Aggie Health — 32k tail latency regression (requests rreq_33452/63/79)

Markus / team — quick findings from a first-pass local repro with the sample payload:
- Reproduced p99 tail >8s on a node configured for hosted multi-tenant runtime when using continuous batching and KV cache sized for 32k windows.
- Memory allocations spike during long forward passes; Python GC cycles create jitter in latency. The batching optimizer is grouping large windows together which increases peak memory pressure.
- Some of the kernel paths we hit fall back to a slower attention kernel for sequences >24k for the model binary currently promoted for this tenant.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered by speed):
1) Turn off continuous-batching for Aggie in the hosted pool for the next 2 hours (cheap, reversible)
2) Apply a max_context cap at the routing layer: reject/redirect requests >24k to fallback variant (lower mem).
3) Short-term: spin a small dedicated pool with 1 larger-memory node and route Aggie there (we can do this in ~30–45m).

I've attached a heap_snapshot.txt captured during repro and a short runbook for #1–#3. If we do (1) + (2) now we should see p99 drop within one routing cycle (~5–10 min).

Laura
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachment: heap_snapshot.txt (text, ~48KB)

Tim — summary and immediate plan: thank you for the sample traces.

What we're doing now (in next 30–60 minutes):
- Disable continuous batching for Aggie in hosted pool (expected p99 improvement within ~10 min)
- Apply routing cap to send >24k requests to a verified fallback variant (quantized)
- If p99 does not recover within 60 minutes we'll route Aggie to a small dedicated pool and keep you updated continuously

Attached is a short mutual action plan (MAP) that documents these steps and a proposed timeline. I've also opened HubSpot record AGH-87 with the incident links and a JIRA ticket (SUP-4521).

Can you confirm you accept the MAP (I can route a DocuSign link) and that 16:00 PDT is a good time for a short war room?

— Markus
